sentences.text: Researchers developed a computational method called optimized multiple temporal interference stimulation (omTIS), which uses multiple electrodes and computer simulations to generate focused electrical fields aimed at distinct brain regions without mutual interference.
This technique was evaluated in computer models, gel-like materials that mimic brain tissue, and live mice.
In these tests, the new method outperformed the standard version of temporal interference stimulation at targeting specific spots and moving the target around.
The authors conclude that this approach offers a way to precisely control widely spread brain circuits without surgery.
